title: Lee-Yang theorem for fermions
authors: Chaithanya Rayudu, Takahiro Misawa, Andrew Zhao, Jun Takahashi
abstract: Lee-Yang theorems are a powerful tool for studying many-body systems, with applications ranging from analyzing phase transitions to proving the efficiency of certain classical and quantum algorithms. In this work, we prove a Lee-Yang zero-freeness theorem for the partition function of a broad class of interacting fermion models, implying the existence of a provably efficient quantum algorithm for estimating their ground-state energies. This class includes several well-known models such as the attractive Hubbard model, repulsive Hubbard model on bipartite graphs, and the interacting Hofstadter model. Our results also rigorously establish the nonexistence of phase transitions in these models in the presence of a nonzero local external field.
summary: This work proves a Lee-Yang zero-freeness theorem for various interacting fermionic models, such as the Hubbard model. This mathematical result implies that the ground-state energies of these complex quantum systems can be estimated using a provably efficient quantum algorithm. It unifies the analysis of several key models under a single rigorous theoretical framework.
main_problem: To prove a Lee-Yang zero-freeness theorem for the partition function of a broad class of interacting fermion models, which has implications for quantum algorithms.
main_result: The theorem establishes that the partition function zeros are constrained in the complex field, implying the existence of a provably efficient quantum algorithm for estimating ground-state energies.
method: The proof involves extending the Lee-Yang theorem from free fermions to interacting models by utilizing Schur product decompositions and analyzing the zero-free regions of the partition function in the complex field.
model_or_system: The study focuses on interacting fermionic Hamiltonians, including the attractive and repulsive Hubbard models on bipartite graphs, and the interacting Hofstadter model.
key_observables: Lee-Yang zeros of the partition function Z(h), ground-state energy, and the spectral gap of the system.
important_parameters: The complex external field parameter h, the inverse temperature beta, and the hopping/interaction strengths U and A.
main_assumptions: The initial class requires attractive interactions and a positive-semidefinite hopping matrix, though extensions exist for repulsive models with strong external fields.
paper_structure: The paper builds from proving zero-freeness for free fermions (Theorem 4) to extending this to interacting fermions via Schur product properties (Theorem 7), and finally applying this to constrain the zeros of the full partition function Z(h) to prove the existence of efficient quantum algorithms (Theorem 2 & 3).
why_interesting: The connection between mathematical properties of the partition function zeros (Lee-Yang theory) and the existence of efficient quantum algorithms provides a deep theoretical link between statistical mechanics and quantum computation.
